gaps.sentence: Thousands of people were forced to ___ their homes.
gaps.hint: a verb is needed after 'to'; meaning: abandon
gaps.explanation: 'Desert' is also a verb meaning to abandon; 'dessert' is only the sweet course of a meal.

gaps.hint: the standard verb with television and sport
gaps.explanation: 'Watch television' is the fixed collocation; 'look' needs 'at', and 'see television' is not used.

gaps.sentence: All ___ must wear identity badges at all times on site.
gaps.explanation: 'Personnel' = the employees of an organisation; 'personal' is an adjective.

gaps.sentence: After twenty years of service, she is one of our most ___ employees.
gaps.explanation: 'A valued member/employee' is someone the organisation appreciates; 'valuable' stresses monetary or practical worth.

gaps.sentence: The sensor is extremely ___ to changes in temperature.
gaps.explanation: 'Sensitive to' reacts readily to something; 'sensible' means showing good judgement.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: She gave me some useful ___ about buying a house.
gaps.hint: a noun is needed after 'some useful'
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is the uncountable noun; 'advise' is the verb. 'Advices' is not standard English.

gaps.sentence: The wine is the perfect ___ to the meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Complement' = something that completes or goes well with; 'compliment' is praise.
